name: Body Systems & Life Processes

objectives.text: Identify major external body parts of common farm animals such as the head, legs, tail, hooves, udder, and comb
Describe the life cycle of a common farm animal from birth or hatching to adulthood
Name the correct terms for the male, female, and young of common livestock species such as bull, cow, heifer, steer, and calf
Describe the basic function of an animal's digestive, respiratory, and circulatory systems in simple terms
Locate major internal organs such as the heart, lungs, stomach, liver, and intestines on a diagram of a livestock animal
Explain how cells, tissues, organs, and body systems are organized to make up an animal's body
Classify farm animals as ruminants or monogastrics based on the structure of their stomachs
Explain how livestock regulate body temperature through panting, sweating, shivering, and hair, wool, or feather cover
Describe the functions of the integumentary system including skin, hair, wool, feathers, hooves, and horns
Describe the parts of the avian digestive tract including the crop, proventriculus, and gizzard and explain the role of each
Diagram the four compartments of a ruminant stomach and explain the path feed follows through each
Describe how the nervous system detects and responds to stimuli to control an animal's movement and behavior
Use industry classification terms to describe external and internal body parts, maturity, and sex of major livestock species
Identify the male and female reproductive organs of cattle, swine, sheep, and poultry and describe the function of each
Analyze the functions of major animal cell structures such as the nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, and cell membrane
Correlate the functions of animal cell structures to growth, development, maintenance, and reproduction in livestock
Analyze how an animal's skeletal, muscular, and respiratory systems work together to support growth and movement
Compare and contrast the digestive anatomy and physiology of ruminant, monogastric, avian, and hindgut fermenting species
Explain the stages of the estrous cycle and the reproductive physiology of gestation and parturition in livestock
Analyze how hormones of the endocrine system regulate growth, lactation, and reproduction in livestock
Evaluate the structural correctness, muscling, and frame of breeding and market livestock to select animals for specific purposes in livestock judging
Evaluate how differences in body systems among ruminant, monogastric, and avian species shape species-specific management practices on a farm

Design an SAE investigation that measures a physiological response such as heart rate, respiration rate, or body temperature in livestock under different conditions and uses the results to recommend a management decision

changes: Kept all six existing objectives as real competencies (reworded only lightly) and anchored the grade 10 and 12 ones to AFNR standards. Filled gaps across the span: life cycle and livestock sex and age terms in the early grades, internal organ location, levels of organization, thermoregulation, integumentary and avian digestive systems, and the nervous system in middle grades. Added high school competencies tied to standards for classification terminology, reproductive organs and estrous physiology, cell structure function and its link to growth and reproduction, comparative digestive anatomy, endocrine regulation, conformation-based selection for livestock judging, and an SAE physiological investigation. Left feeding and rations, disease and biosecurity, and welfare and veterinary procedures to the sibling sub-topics.
